name: Inkflow
author: E. T. Carter
description: Drops of luminous ink released into still dark water, seen side on. Each drop sinks as a column that mushrooms at its head, billows along its flanks and sheds thin tendrils behind it, then thins to haze as a fresh drop falls. The pigment separates as it spreads, so the dense core, the mid body and the thinnest fringe each carry a different palette colour along every billowing edge.

params.label: Cadence
params.effect: How fast the drops sink, spread and dissolve; 0 holds the plumes still.

params.label: Turbulence
params.effect: How hard the water folds the ink; 0 is smooth laminar columns, high is heavily billowed.

params.label: Diffusion
params.effect: How wide the ink diffuses as it sinks; low is thin threads, high is broad soft clouds.

params.label: Tendrils
params.effect: Strength of the fine filaments trailing around each column; 0 leaves only the smooth body.

params.label: Separation
params.effect: How far the pigment separates into distinct colours between core, body and fringe; 0 is one flat ink.

params.label: Mouse influence
params.effect: How strongly the pointer pushes the ink aside; 0 ignores the mouse.
